sanskrit.deva:
यत्तच्छुक्रं महज्ज्योतिर्दीप्यमानं महद्यशः ।
यद्वै देवा उपासते यस्मादर्को विराजते ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:

yad vai devā upāsate yasmād arko virājate |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 1 ||

padaccheda.deva: यत् तत् शुक्रम् महत् ज्योतिः दीप्यमानम् महत् यशः यत् वै देवाः उपासते यस्मात् अर्कः विराजते योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: That which is pure, the great light, shining, the great glory; which the gods worship; from which the sun shines. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the adhyāya: with ‘avāraṇīyaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt’ and what follows (3.22–23) the nature of Brahman was settled, and with ‘tad ātmavit paśyati jñānayogāt’ the seeing of the Self by the yoga of knowledge was taught. Now he shows its nature once more and says that yogins see that form.

Śaṅkara: yat: that which the knower of Brahman sees by the yoga of knowledge, knowing which men become immortal. śukram: pure, free from ignorance and the other faults. The great light, because it makes everything known (‘tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti’). dīpyamānam: radiant. mahad yaśaḥ (‘tasya nāma mahad yaśaḥ’). devāḥ: Indra and the other gods worship it (‘taṃ devā jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āyur hopāsate 'mṛtam’). From Brahman, the supreme light, the sun shines (‘yena sūryas tapati tejaseddhaḥ’). Such a supreme Self, the eternal Lord, yogins alone see, not those without the yoga of knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:

तच्छुक्रं ज्योतिषां मध्येऽतप्तं तपति तापनम् ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ २ ॥

padaccheda.deva: शुक्रात् ब्रह्म प्रभवति ब्रह्म शुक्रेण वर्धते तत् शुक्रम् ज्योतिषाम् मध्ये अतप्तम् तपति तापनम् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: From the pure (Brahman) arises Brahman (called Hiraṇyagarbha); (that) Brahman grows by the pure (as Virāj). That pure (Brahman), in the midst of the lights, not lit (by them), shines (of itself), and makes them shine. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows that Hiraṇyagarbha and the rest arise from the supreme Brahman itself.

Śaṅkara: from the pure Brahman spoken of before, the Brahman called Hiraṇyagarbha arises; arisen, it grows by the pure in the form of Virāj. That pure Brahman, in the midst of the sun and the other lights, not lit (ataptam, aprakāśitam) by them, shines of itself and makes them too shine. Him who is not lit by others, who lights all and shines of himself, the Lord, yogins alone see.

योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ३ ॥

haranti pūrṇāt pūrṇaṃ ca pūrṇenaivāvaśiṣyate |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 3 ||

padaccheda.deva: पूर्णात् पूर्णम् उद्धरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णम् प्रचक्षते हरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णम् च पूर्णेन एव अवशिष्यते योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: From the full (the supreme Self) they draw out the full (as the jīva); (the wise) declare (it) full, being from the full. And from the full (standing as the jīva) they take the full (the Self, out of the two bodies); it remains with the full alone (as Brahman). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now gives the sense of the pūrṇa sentence (pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam).

Śaṅkara: from the supreme Self, full, unlimited in place, time and thing, they draw out the full itself as the jīva. Because it is drawn out from the full, the wise declare this nature of the jīva also full. And from the full that stands as the jīva they take the full: the Self alone, which has entered body, senses and the rest, they separate from them and draw out, the witness of them, the innermost, from the two bodies. Then it remains with that root, the full bliss so drawn out: it is joined with Brahman, the full bliss, and abides as Brahman, consciousness, being and bliss, without a second.

Śaṅkara: or the reading is ‘pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate’: when they separate the Self from body and senses and draw out their witness, the innermost, from the two bodies, the full alone remains. So the śruti: ‘pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṃ pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate, pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate’. Its sense: adaḥ, full, is Brahman, the cause of the world, meant by the word tat; idam, full, is the inner Self, pointed to by the word tvam. How are the meanings of tat and tvam full? Because the full is drawn out (udricyate) from the unlimited full as jīva and Īśvara, both are full. pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya: taking the full form of what stands as tat and tvam, that is, having purified the meanings of the two words; then the full Brahman alone remains, one becomes the full Brahman. Him whose nature is the full, the supreme Self, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:

आद्ध्रीचीः सविषूचीर्वसानावुभौ बिभर्ति पृथिवीं दिवं च ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ४ ॥

padaccheda.iast: āpaḥ atha adbhyaḥ salilam tasya madhye ubhau devau śiśriyāte antarikṣe āddhrīcīḥ sa-viṣūcīḥ vasānau ubhau bibharti pṛthivīm divam ca yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: आपः अथ अद्भ्यः सलिलम् तस्य मध्ये उभौ देवौ शिश्रियाते अन्तरिक्षे आद्ध्रीचीः स-विषूचीः वसानौ उभौ बिभर्ति पृथिवीम् दिवम् च योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: The waters (were made first); then from the waters the water (the gross body); in its midst, in the space (of the heart), the two gods (the jīva and the supreme Self) dwell. Clothed in the quarters with the intermediate quarters, the two bear: (the one) the earth, (the other) heaven. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now gives the sense of the mantra ‘dvā suparṇā’.

Śaṅkara: from this supreme Self the waters were made first (Manu: ‘apa eva sasarjādau’); the word ‘waters’ stands for the five elements, and with it the subtle creation is told. Then from the waters made before, ‘water’, the gross body and the rest, made of the five elements, was made. In the midst of that water, which stands as the body, in antarikṣa, the space of the heart, the two gods, the jīva and the supreme Self, shining by nature, dwell.

Śaṅkara: not only in that space: āddhrīcīḥ are the quarters, so called because they go (añcanti) facing, being held (dhriyamāṇāḥ) or standing; viṣūcīḥ are the intermediate quarters, from going all ways (viṣvak); saviṣūcīḥ, with them, are all the quarters, east and the rest; vasānau: covering them. ubhau bibharti pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca: the one, the jīva, not knowing his own natural being as Brahman, consciousness, being and bliss without a second, and taking the not-self, the body and the rest, for the self, bears the ‘earth’: the body and the rest, made of the elements and their products, of pleasure and pain, as his karma has earned. The other bears ‘heaven’: his own Self, whose nature is light. He cites ‘dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā …’. Him who by his own māyā makes himself into endless distinctions, prāṇa and the rest, enters within and abides looking on, the Lord, yogins alone see.
The edition prints āddhrīcīḥ (आद्ध्रीचीः) in the verse and in the bhāṣya; the lemma is given as ādhrīcī, after Śaṅkara's derivation from ā-dhṛ and añc.

केतुमन्तं वहन्त्यश्वास्तं दिव्यमजरं दिवि ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ५ ॥

ketumantaṃ vahanty aśvās taṃ divyam ajaraṃ divi |

ketumantaṃ vahanty aśvās taṃ divyam ajaraṃ divi

padaccheda.deva: चक्रे रथस्य तिष्ठन्तम् ध्रुवस्य अव्यय-कर्मणः केतुमन्तम् वहन्ति अश्वाः तम् दिव्यम् अजरम् दिवि योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Him who stands on the wheel (the body) of the chariot of the steadfast (Lord) whose work is imperishable, (the man) of understanding, divine, ageless: the horses (the senses) carry him into heaven (Brahman). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows the man of knowledge abiding in his own Self.

Śaṅkara: dhruvasyāvyayakarmaṇaḥ: of the supreme Lord, who stands as Īśvara. rathasya: of his body, which stands as the three worlds. cakre: in the body, which moves (caṅkramaṇa). ketumantam: possessed of understanding (prajñāvantam), and therefore divine, not of Prakṛti, free of old age, death and the rest. divi: in Brahman, the full bliss, which is light and stands as knowledge that neither rises nor sets. There the horses, the senses, carry him. The sense is this: though the senses by their nature go to objects only, drawn in by the charioteer that is understanding (vijñāna) they carry the man of understanding into heaven, not to outward objects. So it is said in the Kaṭha (1.3.3–4): ‘ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu …’. The supreme Self into which they carry him by austerity, the Lord, yogins alone see.

translations.text: His form does not stand in likeness (to anything); no one sees him with the eye. Those who know him (as ‘this I am’) by the understanding, by the mind and by the heart, they become immortal. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: nothing is like him, he says.

Śaṅkara: the form of this supreme Self does not stand in likeness with another: nothing is like him (‘na tasya pratimā asti yasya nāma mahad yaśaḥ’), and so he is no object of comparison or the like. No one sees him, the innermost supreme Self, with the eye. How then do they see? By manīṣā, the deciding faculty; by manas, whose nature is resolve and doubt; and by hṛd, the heart, as the means: ‘by the heart’ is said because the supreme Self is found nowhere but in the heart. Or: not by mind and understanding alone, but favoured by the supreme Lord who dwells in the heart. Or: hṛdā is the heart, the supreme Self itself; so the śruti explains the word hṛdaya of the Self in the heart (‘sa eṣa ātmā hṛdi tasyaitad eva niruktaṃ hṛdayam iti …’), and shows that the gaining of the Self depends on him (‘yasya deve parā bhaktiḥ …’). Those who know him as ‘this I am’ become immortal, free of death. Him, knowing whom they become immortal, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
द्वादश पूगाः सरितो देवरक्षिता मध्वीशते ।
तदनुविधायिनस्तदा संचरन्ति घोरम् ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dvādaśa pūgāḥ sarito devarakṣitā madhv īśate |
tadanuvidhāyinas tadā saṃcaranti ghoram |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 7 ||

tadanuvidhāyinas tadā saṃcaranti ghoram
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: dvādaśa pūgāḥ saritaḥ deva-rakṣitāḥ madhu īśate tad-anuvidhāyinaḥ tadā saṃcaranti ghoram yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: द्वादश पूगाः सरितः देव-रक्षिताः मधु ईशते तद्-अनुविधायिनः तदा संचरन्ति घोरम् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: The twelve groups, flowing streams guarded by the God (the supreme Self), rule over the honey (each its own object); then those who follow them wander in the dreadful (saṃsāra). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now says that the going of the senses to their objects is for harm.

Śaṅkara: the twelve groups are the organs of action and of knowledge, the mind the eleventh, the understanding the twelfth; each is called a group with regard to the many persons. saritaḥ: flowing. devarakṣitāḥ: guarded by the God, the supreme Self. madhu: the object, which is like honey. īśate: they govern it, each enjoying its own object without confusion. When they so enjoy, those who follow them, intent on objects, wander in the dreadful saṃsāra. Therefore one should withdraw the senses from their objects and bring them under control in oneself. The God guarded by whom they rule over the honey, yogins alone see.

योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ८ ॥

īśānaḥ sarvabhūteṣu havirbhūtam akalpayat |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 8 ||

lines.iast: tad ardhamāsaṃ pibati saṃcitaṃ bhramaro madhu
īśānaḥ sarvabhūteṣu havirbhūtam akalpayat
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: tat ardha-māsam pibati saṃcitam bhramaraḥ madhu īśānaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu haviḥ-bhūtam akalpayat yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: तत् अर्ध-मासम् पिबति संचितम् भ्रमरः मधु ईशानः सर्व-भूतेषु हविः-भूतम् अकल्पयत् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: The bee drinks for half a month the honey gathered (for half a month): (so the one in saṃsāra enjoys in another birth the karma gathered in a former one). The Lord prepared in all beings what has become the offering. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: further, the illustration and what it illustrates are both told here.

Śaṅkara: as the bee, the honey-maker, drinks for half a month the honey gathered over half a month, so this ‘bee’, the one in saṃsāra, so called because he wanders, drinks the honey of objects gathered over half a month: he enjoys in another birth the karma gathered in a former birth. Objection: karma whose fruit is in this world may bring its fruit, since the fruit follows the act; but how can karma whose fruit is in the other world bring it, since karma perishes? To this he says īśānaḥ: the fault would hold if the fruit came from karma alone; but the Lord, the supreme Īśvara, regarding the effort made, prepared in all creatures, according to their karma, the food and the rest that has become the offering, of the agnihotra of the breath and of the other (rites). The Lord who prepared this, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
हिरण्यपर्णमश्वत्थमभिपत्य ह्यपक्षकाः ।
तत्र ते पक्षिणो भूत्वा प्रपतन्ति यथासुखम् ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hiraṇyaparṇam aśvattham abhipatya hy apakṣakāḥ |
tatra te pakṣiṇo bhūtvā prapatanti yathāsukham |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 9 ||

lines.iast: hiraṇyaparṇam aśvattham abhipatya hy apakṣakāḥ
tatra te pakṣiṇo bhūtvā prapatanti yathāsukham
lines.deva: तत्र ते पक्षिणो भूत्वा प्रपतन्ति यथासुखम्

lines.iast: yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: hiraṇya-parṇam aśvattham abhipatya hi apakṣakāḥ tatra te pakṣiṇaḥ bhūtvā prapatanti yathāsukham yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: हिरण्य-पर्णम् अश्वत्थम् अभिपत्य हि अपक्षकाः तत्र ते पक्षिणः भूत्वा प्रपतन्ति यथासुखम् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: The wingless (without the wings of knowledge), having flown to the holy fig tree with golden leaves (the body of a brāhmaṇa or the like, joined to the Veda), become winged there (men of knowledge) and fly away at their ease (are freed). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: do these eaters of honey, whirling about, go on turning for ever, or do they gain knowledge and become free? To this he says:

Śaṅkara: the wingless are those without the wings of knowledge, the eaters of honey who keep turning. hiraṇyaparṇa: the fig tree whose leaves are hiraṇya, that is, beneficial (hita) and delightful (ramaṇīya); so the Lord Vāsudeva says (Gītā 15.1): ‘chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni’. abhipatya: having climbed it, that is, having gained the body of a brāhmaṇa or the like, which is joined to the Veda. There, in that very body, they become winged, men of knowledge (the Brāhmaṇa: ‘ye vai vidvāṃsas te pakṣiṇo ye 'vidvāṃsas te 'pakṣāḥ’), and fly away at ease: they become free. Him, knowing whom they fly away, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
अपानं गिरति प्राणः प्राणं गिरति चन्द्रमाः ।
आदित्यो गिरते चन्द्रमादित्यं गिरते परः ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
apānaṃ girati prāṇaḥ prāṇaṃ girati candramāḥ |
ādityo girate candram ādityaṃ girate paraḥ |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 10 ||

lines.iast: apānaṃ girati prāṇaḥ prāṇaṃ girati candramāḥ
lines.deva: अपानं गिरति प्राणः प्राणं गिरति चन्द्रमाः

lines.iast: ādityo girate candram ādityaṃ girate paraḥ
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: apānam girati prāṇaḥ prāṇam girati candramāḥ ādityaḥ girate candram ādityam girate paraḥ yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: अपानम् गिरति प्राणः प्राणम् गिरति चन्द्रमाः आदित्यः गिरते चन्द्रम् आदित्यम् गिरते परः योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Prāṇa swallows apāna; the moon (the mind) swallows prāṇa; the sun (the understanding) swallows the moon; the supreme (Brahman) swallows the sun. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows yoga.

Śaṅkara: prāṇa swallows, withdraws, apāna. The moon, the mind, withdraws prāṇa: the moon is the deity of the mind, so the word ‘moon’ means the mind. The sun, the understanding, swallows that moon, the mind: the sun is the deity of the understanding. The supreme, the supreme Brahman, swallows that sun, the understanding. This is what is said: at the time of absorption (samādhi), having withdrawn apāna into prāṇa, prāṇa into the mind, the mind into the understanding and the understanding into the supreme Self, one abides as Brahman, one's own nature, consciousness, being and bliss without a second.

sanskrit.deva:
एकं पादं नोत्क्षिपति सलिलाद्धंस उच्चरन् ।
तं चेत्सततमुत्क्षिपेन्न मृत्युर्नामृतं भवेत् ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ekaṃ pādaṃ notkṣipati salilād dhaṃsa uccaran |
taṃ cet satatam utkṣipen na mṛtyur nāmṛtaṃ bhavet |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 11 ||

lines.iast: ekaṃ pādaṃ notkṣipati salilād dhaṃsa uccaran
taṃ cet satatam utkṣipen na mṛtyur nāmṛtaṃ bhavet
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: ekam pādam na utkṣipati salilāt haṃsaḥ uccaran tam cet satatam utkṣipet na mṛtyuḥ na amṛtam bhavet yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: एकम् पादम् न उत्क्षिपति सलिलात् हंसः उच्चरन् तम् चेत् सततम् उत्क्षिपेत् न मृत्युः न अमृतम् भवेत् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Rising from the water (saṃsāra), the swan (the supreme Self) does not lift out one foot (the jīva). If he were to lift out that ever-moving (foot), there would be neither death nor deathlessness. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows the supreme abiding as the jīva.

Śaṅkara: haṃsa is the supreme Self, because he destroys (hanti) ignorance and its effect. salilāt: from saṃsāra, made of the elements and their products. uccaran: moving above, staying outside saṃsāra. He does not lift out, withdraw, the one foot called the jīva: he stays as the counterpart in every form (‘rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpaḥ’; the Kaṭha: ‘ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā’). Why does he not lift it out? If he were to lift out that foot, the jīva, which goes on without break (satatam, santatayāyinam), that is, if he did not by his own māyā make himself into endless distinctions, prāṇa and the rest, enter them and abide as the jīva, there would be no death, no saṃsāra, the harm of birth, death and the rest, since there would be no jīva in saṃsāra; nor would there be deathlessness, liberation, since what had not entered could not be seen. For this very purpose the śruti shows the entering (‘rūpaṃ rūpam’). So the Atharvaṇa śruti gives the same verse (‘ekaṃ pādaṃ notkṣipati salilād dhaṃsa uccaran, sa ced utkṣipet pādaṃ na mṛtyur nāmṛtaṃ bhavet’) and ‘ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti’. Him who abides as the jīva in the form of a foot and in three feet as Brahman, consciousness, being and bliss without a second, the supreme Self, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा लिङ्गस्य योगेन स याति नित्यम् ।
तमीशमीड्यमनुकल्पमाद्यं पश्यन्ति मूढा न विराजमानम् ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā liṅgasya yogena sa yāti nityam |
tam īśam īḍyam anukalpam ādyaṃ paśyanti mūḍhā na virājamānam |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 12 ||

lines.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā liṅgasya yogena sa yāti nityam
lines.deva: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा लिङ्गस्य योगेन स याति नित्यम्

lines.iast: tam īśam īḍyam anukalpam ādyaṃ paśyanti mūḍhā na virājamānam
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.deva: अङ्गुष्ठ-मात्रः पुरुषः अन्तरात्मा लिङ्गस्य योगेन सः याति नित्यम् तम् ईशम् ईड्यम् अनुकल्पम् आद्यम् पश्यन्ति मूढाः न विराजमानम् योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Puruṣa, the inner Self, the size of a thumb through union with the subtle body, ever goes (from birth to birth): (because) the deluded do not see him, the lord, to be praised, who enters all and shapes (it), the first, the shining. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: by what limiting adjunct, then, does the supreme abide as the foot? Asking this, he shows the jīva as the supreme itself with the subtle body (liṅga) as its adjunct.

Śaṅkara: he alone, being, consciousness and bliss without a second, the inner Self of all beings, Puruṣa, the full, the supreme Self, through union with the subtle body becomes the size of a thumb, limited to that measure, and goes, transmigrates, ever. Why does he so transmigrate? Because the deluded, who do not discriminate and take the two bodies for the self, do not see him: the lord of all, to be praised, anukalpa (he enters all and shapes it by himself), the first (who was in the beginning), shining. Through not knowing the Self as Brahman they transmigrate. Him, not seeing whom they transmigrate, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
गूहन्ति सर्पा इव गह्वरेषु क्षयं नीत्वा स्वेन वृत्तेन मर्त्यान् ।
ते विप्रमुह्यन्ति जना विमूढास्तैर्दत्ता भोगा मोहयन्ते भवाय ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gūhanti sarpā iva gahvareṣu kṣayaṃ nītvā svena vṛttena martyān |
te vipramuhyanti janā vimūḍhās tair dattā bhogā mohayante bhavāya |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 13 ||

lines.iast: gūhanti sarpā iva gahvareṣu kṣayaṃ nītvā svena vṛttena martyān
lines.deva: गूहन्ति सर्पा इव गह्वरेषु क्षयं नीत्वा स्वेन वृत्तेन मर्त्यान्

lines.deva: ते विप्रमुह्यन्ति जना विमूढास्तैर्दत्ता भोगा मोहयन्ते भवाय

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Like snakes in their holes, (the senses) hide (themselves), having led mortals to destruction by their own conduct (giving the poison of objects). Those people, bewildered, are utterly deluded; the enjoyments given by them delude (men) for becoming (birth and death). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now shows that the senses and their objects are the cause of harm.

Śaṅkara: as snakes come out of their holes, by their conduct, the giving of poison, lead mortals to destruction and then hide themselves in the holes, so the snakes that are the senses, lying in the ear and the rest, come out of them, by their own conduct, the giving of the poison of objects, lead mortals to destruction and hide themselves in the holes. Those people, overcome by the poison of objects, are utterly deluded: they know nothing beyond (the objects), as the śruti says, ‘yathā priyayā striyā saṃpariṣvaktaḥ’. The enjoyments given by the snakes of the senses, objects like poison, delude mortals: they are the cause of delusion again and again; and this deluding by objects is for bhava, the saṃsāra of womb, birth, old age and death. Him, the blameless, who shapes all, the first, not seeing whom they are deluded, blinded by the poison of objects, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:

समानमेतदमृतस्येतरस्य युक्तास्तत्र मध्व उत्सं समापुः ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १४ ॥

samānam etad amṛtasyetarasya yuktās tatra madhva utsaṃ samāpuḥ |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 14 ||

lines.iast: asādhanā vāpi sasādhanā vā samānam etad dṛśyate mānuṣeṣu
lines.deva: असाधना वापि ससाधना वा समानमेतद्दृश्यते मानुषेषु

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Whether without the means or with the means, this (Self) is seen the same among men; this is the same for deathlessness and for the other (saṃsāra). Those joined (to the means) have reached there (in the supreme abode of Viṣṇu) the spring of honey (Brahman, the full bliss). Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he states what liberation is for the men of knowledge.

Śaṅkara: in those without the means, without calm, restraint and the rest, and in those with them, the same, common nature of the Self is seen among men. It is the same too for deathlessness, liberation, and for the other, saṃsāra, whether (the means) are there or not. Among them, those who are joined to the means, calm, restraint and the rest, reach there, in the supreme abode of Viṣṇu, the spring of honey: they reach Brahman, the full bliss. The spring, the full bliss, which the joined reach, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:

योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १५ ॥

mā te brāhmī laghutām ādadhīta prajñānaṃ syān nāma dhīrā labhante |

lines.deva: उभौ लोकौ विद्यया व्याप्य यान्ति तदाहुतं चाहुतमग्निहोत्रम्

lines.iast: mā te brāhmī laghutām ādadhīta prajñānaṃ syān nāma dhīrā labhante
lines.deva: मा ते ब्राह्मी लघुतामादधीत प्रज्ञानं स्यान्नाम धीरा लभन्ते

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Having pervaded both worlds by knowledge, they go to That; (therefore) the agnihotra not offered is offered. Your knowledge of Brahman will not bring lightness (mortality, as action does): it would be named ‘consciousness’ (Brahman); the wise gain it. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara: ubhau lokau: this world and the other; pervading them by the knowledge whose object is Brahman as the Self, one goes to That, Brahman, the full bliss. Since one goes pervading both worlds by knowledge, the agnihotra not offered is offered by this knowledge of the Self, offered directly (ābhimukhyena): all the fruit of the agnihotra and the other rites is gained by this alone. Since one pervades both worlds by knowledge, and the agnihotra not offered is offered, therefore your knowledge whose object is Brahman does not bring lightness, mortality, as action does; rather it makes consciousness, the supreme Self beyond darkness, one's own self. When one engaged in the knowledge of Brahman knows the supreme Self as the self, the name ‘consciousness’ belongs to it: the name ‘Brahman’ (the śruti: ‘prajñānaṃ brahma’). That Brahman, consciousness, the wise, men of understanding, gain. Him, Brahman, consciousness, whom the wise gain, yogins alone see.
Śaṅkara glosses the verse's yānti with a singular, yāti; and he reads tat as the goal (‘That, Brahman, the full bliss’), joining the agnihotra clause to it by ‘therefore’.

sanskrit.deva:
एवंरूपो महानात्मा पावकं पुरुषो गिरन् ।
यो वै तं पुरुषं वेद तस्येहात्मा न रिष्यते ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
evaṃrūpo mahān ātmā pāvakaṃ puruṣo giran |
yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ veda tasyehātmā na riṣyate |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 16 ||

lines.iast: evaṃrūpo mahān ātmā pāvakaṃ puruṣo giran
yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ veda tasyehātmā na riṣyate
lines.deva: यो वै तं पुरुषं वेद तस्येहात्मा न रिष्यते

lines.iast: yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: evam-rūpaḥ mahān ātmā pāvakam puruṣaḥ giran yaḥ vai tam puruṣam veda tasya iha ātmā na riṣyate yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: एवम्-रूपः महान् आत्मा पावकम् पुरुषः गिरन् यः वै तम् पुरुषम् वेद तस्य इह आत्मा न रिष्यते योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Of such a form (Brahman, consciousness alone), Puruṣa, swallowing the fire (the cause, with its effects), (becomes) the great Self. He who knows that Puruṣa, his self does not perish here. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara: he who abides of such a form, as Brahman whose only taste is consciousness, that self becomes great: becomes Brahman itself. pāvakam: the fire, the cause, whose form is to withdraw all; swallowing it, withdrawing into himself the effect with its cause. He who knows that Puruṣa, whose only taste is knowledge, the full, who dwells in the city (puriśaya), directly, as ‘this I am’: for him, as he knows the supreme Self, which is consciousness, as the self, the self does not perish here, in this very body; for the knower does not depart, and perishing is caused by departing. So the śruti shows, with a question, that he does not depart: ‘ud asmāt prāṇāḥ krāmanti āho neti neti hovāca yājñavalkyo 'traiva samavanīyante’, and ‘na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti ya evaṃ veda’. Him, knowing whom one does not perish, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मात्सदा सत्कृतः स्यान्न मृत्युरमृतं कुतः ।
सत्यानृते सत्यसमानुबन्धिनी सतश्च योनिरसतश्चैक एव ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmāt sadā satkṛtaḥ syān na mṛtyur amṛtaṃ kutaḥ |
satyānṛte satyasamānubandhinī sataś ca yonir asataś caika eva |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 17 ||

lines.iast: tasmāt sadā satkṛtaḥ syān na mṛtyur amṛtaṃ kutaḥ
satyānṛte satyasamānubandhinī sataś ca yonir asataś caika eva
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt sadā sat-kṛtaḥ syāt na mṛtyuḥ amṛtam kutaḥ satya-anṛte satya-samānubandhinī sataḥ ca yoniḥ asataḥ ca ekaḥ eva yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् सदा सत्-कृतः स्यात् न मृत्युः अमृतम् कुतः सत्य-अनृते सत्य-समानुबन्धिनी सतः च योनिः असतः च एकः एव योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: Therefore one should always be ‘honoured with being’ (think oneself Brahman); (for him) there is no death: whence deathlessness? Truth and untruth are bound to the true; the source of what is and of what is not is one alone. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: since from knowing That alone there is no perishing of the self —

Śaṅkara: sadā: at all times, day and night. satkṛtaḥ syāt: he who thinks of himself as Brahman, being, consciousness and bliss without a second, is ever ‘made sat’; for him there is no death, no saṃsāra of birth and death. amṛtaṃ kutaḥ: deathlessness depends on death; where death is not, how could it arise? (the śruti: ‘mṛtyur nāsty amṛtaṃ kutaḥ’). Truth and untruth exist bound to the true: bound to the one substrate, the true in the highest sense, as the snake to the rope. How is this known? Because they declare the one Brahman without a second the source of the ‘what is’, the worldly, and of the ‘what is not’, the merely conventional, such as silver (seen in shell); therefore truth and untruth are bound to the true, their cause. Him, by the knowledge of whose truth as the self death is destroyed, to whom truth and untruth are bound, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा न दृश्यतेऽसौ हृदये निविष्टः ।
अजश्चरो दिवारात्रमतन्द्रितश्च स तं मत्वा कविरास्ते प्रसन्नः ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā na dṛśyate 'sau hṛdaye niviṣṭaḥ |
ajaś caro divārātram atandritaś ca sa taṃ matvā kavir āste prasannaḥ || 18 ||

lines.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā na dṛśyate 'sau hṛdaye niviṣṭaḥ
lines.deva: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा न दृश्यतेऽसौ हृदये निविष्टः

lines.iast: ajaś caro divārātram atandritaś ca sa taṃ matvā kavir āste prasannaḥ
lines.deva: अजश्चरो दिवारात्रमतन्द्रितश्च स तं मत्वा कविरास्ते प्रसन्नः

padaccheda.iast: aṅguṣṭha-mātraḥ puruṣaḥ antarātmā na dṛśyate asau hṛdaye niviṣṭaḥ ajaḥ caraḥ divārātram atandritaḥ ca saḥ tam matvā kaviḥ āste prasannaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अङ्गुष्ठ-मात्रः पुरुषः अन्तरात्मा न दृश्यते असौ हृदये निविष्टः अजः चरः दिवारात्रम् अतन्द्रितः च सः तम् मत्वा कविः आस्ते प्रसन्नः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Puruṣa, the inner Self, the size of a thumb, settled in the heart (having created the world), unborn, moving (the self of all that moves and does not move), is not seen (as he is). Unwearied day and night (coming out of the five sheaths), having known him, the wise man remains serene.

notes: Śaṅkara: having created the world, from space down to the body, he has entered the heart; unborn, cara: the self of the moving and the unmoving; he is not seen in his own nature, consciousness, being and bliss without a second. Unwearied day and night, having come out of the five sheaths and known him, the inner Self of all, the wise man remains serene: he has gained his end.
Śaṅkara joins divārātram atandritaḥ with the wise man, not with the Self. The verse has no refrain in the edition.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्माच्च वायुरायातस्तस्मिंश्च प्रलयस्तथा ।
तस्मादग्निश्च सोमश्च तस्माच्च प्राण आगतः ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmāc ca vāyur āyātas tasmiṃś ca pralayas tathā |
tasmād agniś ca somaś ca tasmāc ca prāṇa āgataḥ || 19 ||

lines.iast: tasmāc ca vāyur āyātas tasmiṃś ca pralayas tathā
tasmād agniś ca somaś ca tasmāc ca prāṇa āgataḥ

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt ca vāyuḥ āyātaḥ tasmin ca pralayaḥ tathā tasmāt agniḥ ca somaḥ ca tasmāt ca prāṇaḥ āgataḥ
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् च वायुः आयातः तस्मिन् च प्रलयः तथा तस्मात् अग्निः च सोमः च तस्मात् च प्राणः आगतः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: From That (Brahman) the wind has come, and in That likewise is (its) dissolution; from That fire and the moon, and from That prāṇa has come.

notes: Śaṅkara gives no comment on this verse and the next singly. Introducing verse 21 he says only that these two verses tell how all this arose from Brahman and dissolves in it.

sanskrit.deva:
तत्प्रतिष्ठा तदमृतं लोकास्तद्ब्रह्म तद्यशः ।
भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात्प्रलयं यान्ति तत्र च ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tat pratiṣṭhā tad amṛtaṃ lokās tad brahma tad yaśaḥ |
bhūtāni jajñire tasmāt pralayaṃ yānti tatra ca || 20 ||

lines.iast: tat pratiṣṭhā tad amṛtaṃ lokās tad brahma tad yaśaḥ
bhūtāni jajñire tasmāt pralayaṃ yānti tatra ca
lines.deva: भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात्प्रलयं यान्ति तत्र च

padaccheda.iast: tat pratiṣṭhā tat amṛtam lokāḥ tat brahma tat yaśaḥ bhūtāni jajñire tasmāt pralayam yānti tatra ca
padaccheda.deva: तत् प्रतिष्ठा तत् अमृतम् लोकाः तत् ब्रह्म तत् यशः भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात् प्रलयम् यान्ति तत्र च

translations.text: That is the support, That the immortal, (That) the worlds, That Brahman, That glory. Beings were born from That, and go to dissolution there.

notes: Śaṅkara, after this verse: by these two verses (19–20) it is said that all this arose from Brahman and dissolves in it; the next verse explains it.

sanskrit.deva:
उभौ च देवौ पृथिवीं दिवं च दिशश्च शुक्रं भुवनं बिभर्ति ।
तस्माद्दिशः सरितश्च स्रवन्ति तस्मात्समुद्रा विहिता महान्तः ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ubhau ca devau pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca diśaś ca śukraṃ bhuvanaṃ bibharti |
tasmād diśaḥ saritaś ca sravanti tasmāt samudrā vihitā mahāntaḥ || 21 ||

lines.iast: ubhau ca devau pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca diśaś ca śukraṃ bhuvanaṃ bibharti
lines.deva: उभौ च देवौ पृथिवीं दिवं च दिशश्च शुक्रं भुवनं बिभर्ति

lines.iast: tasmād diśaḥ saritaś ca sravanti tasmāt samudrā vihitā mahāntaḥ
lines.deva: तस्माद्दिशः सरितश्च स्रवन्ति तस्मात्समुद्रा विहिता महान्तः

padaccheda.iast: ubhau ca devau pṛthivīm divam ca diśaḥ ca śukram bhuvanam bibharti tasmāt diśaḥ saritaḥ ca sravanti tasmāt samudrāḥ vihitāḥ mahāntaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उभौ च देवौ पृथिवीम् दिवम् च दिशः च शुक्रम् भुवनम् बिभर्ति तस्मात् दिशः सरितः च स्रवन्ति तस्मात् समुद्राः विहिताः महान्तः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: The pure (Brahman) bears both the gods, the earth and heaven, the quarters and the world. From That the quarters and the rivers flow; from That the great oceans were made.

notes: Śaṅkara: the sense of the verse is plain.
The edition prints tasmādiśaḥ (तस्मादिशः); read tasmād diśaḥ (तस्माद्दिशः).

sanskrit.deva:
यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां पक्षानाहृत्य संपतेत् ।
नान्तं गच्छेत्कारणस्य यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः ।
योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम् ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ pakṣān āhṛtya saṃpatet |
nāntaṃ gacchet kāraṇasya yady api syān manojavaḥ |
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam || 22 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ pakṣān āhṛtya saṃpatet
nāntaṃ gacchet kāraṇasya yady api syān manojavaḥ
yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ sahasram sahasrāṇām pakṣān āhṛtya saṃpatet na antam gacchet kāraṇasya yadi api syāt manaḥ-javaḥ yoginaḥ tam prapaśyanti bhagavantam sanātanam
padaccheda.deva: यः सहस्रम् सहस्राणाम् पक्षान् आहृत्य संपतेत् न अन्तम् गच्छेत् कारणस्य यदि अपि स्यात् मनः-जवः योगिनः तम् प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तम् सनातनम्

translations.text: He who, taking a thousand thousands of wings, should fly, would not reach the end of the cause (the supreme Self), even if he were swift as the mind. Yogins (alone) see him, the eternal Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he now tells of the endlessness of Brahman.

Śaṅkara: a man who took a thousand thousands of wings, making them his own, and flew, many times over, even for crores of kalpas, would not reach the end of the cause, the supreme Self, the cause of all; even if he were swift as the mind, he would not reach its end. Since he would not reach the end, the supreme Self is endless. Him, the endless supreme Self, yogins alone see.

sanskrit.deva:
अदर्शने तिष्ठति रूपमस्य पश्यन्ति चैनं सुसमिद्धसत्त्वाः ।
हीनो मनीषी मनसाभिपश्येद्य एनं विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
adarśane tiṣṭhati rūpam asya paśyanti cainaṃ susamiddhasattvāḥ |
hīno manīṣī manasābhipaśyed ya enaṃ vidur amṛtās te bhavanti || 23 ||

lines.iast: adarśane tiṣṭhati rūpam asya paśyanti cainaṃ susamiddhasattvāḥ
lines.deva: अदर्शने तिष्ठति रूपमस्य पश्यन्ति चैनं सुसमिद्धसत्त्वाः

lines.iast: hīno manīṣī manasābhipaśyed ya enaṃ vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
lines.deva: हीनो मनीषी मनसाभिपश्येद्य एनं विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: adarśane tiṣṭhati rūpam asya paśyanti ca enam su-samiddha-sattvāḥ hīnaḥ manīṣī manasā abhipaśyet ye enam viduḥ amṛtāḥ te bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: अदर्शने तिष्ठति रूपम् अस्य पश्यन्ति च एनम् सु-समिद्ध-सत्त्वाः हीनः मनीषी मनसा अभिपश्येत् ये एनम् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति

translations.text: His form stands out of sight; yet those whose mind is well kindled (made clean by sacrifice and the rest) see him. (Therefore) the wise man, bereft (of the stains of passion and the rest), should see (him) with the mind. Those who know him (as ‘I am’) become immortal.

notes: Śaṅkara: adarśane: in a domain not fit for seeing his form stands (the śruti: ‘na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya’). Though it stands where it cannot be seen, they see the supreme Self. Who? Those whose inner organ (sattva) is well and rightly kindled, being made spotless by sacrifice and the rest. Since this is so, the wise man, hīna, free from the stains of passion, hatred and the rest, of pure mind, should see with the mind. Those who know this supreme Self as ‘I am’ become immortal, free of death.
The verse has no refrain in the edition.

sanskrit.deva:
इमं यः सर्वभूतेषु आत्मानमनुपश्यति ।
अन्यत्रान्यत्र युक्तेषु स किं शोचेत्ततः परम् ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
imaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ātmānam anupaśyati |
anyatrānyatra yukteṣu sa kiṃ śocet tataḥ param || 24 ||

lines.iast: imaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ātmānam anupaśyati
anyatrānyatra yukteṣu sa kiṃ śocet tataḥ param
lines.deva: अन्यत्रान्यत्र युक्तेषु स किं शोचेत्ततः परम्

padaccheda.iast: imam yaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu ātmānam anupaśyati anyatra anyatra yukteṣu saḥ kim śocet tataḥ param
padaccheda.deva: इमम् यः सर्व-भूतेषु आत्मानम् अनुपश्यति अन्यत्र अन्यत्र युक्तेषु सः किम् शोचेत् ततः परम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. loc. pl.

translations.text: He who sees this Self in all beings, joined (to bodies and senses) here and there, why should he grieve after that?

notes: Śaṅkara: this, the innermost of all; he who sees it in all beings, in all creatures. In what kind of beings? anyatrānyatra yukteṣu: in those joined to body, senses and the rest, who take the body and the rest for the self. Seeing his self in all beings, why should he grieve after that? Seeing the Self that dwells in all beings, he has gained his end and does not grieve (the śruti: ‘tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvam anupaśyataḥ’).

sanskrit.deva:
यथोदपाने महति सर्वतःसंप्लुतोदके ।
एवं भूतेषु सर्वेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathodapāne mahati sarvataḥsaṃplutodake |
evaṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣu brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ || 25 ||

lines.iast: yathodapāne mahati sarvataḥsaṃplutodake
evaṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣu brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ

padaccheda.iast: yathā udapāne mahati sarvataḥ-saṃpluta-udake evam bhūteṣu sarveṣu brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ
padaccheda.deva: यथा उदपाने महति सर्वतः-संप्लुत-उदके एवम् भूतेषु सर्वेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः

words.meaning: flooded with water on every side

translations.text: As (there is no need) of a great well when (all is) flooded with water on every side, so (there is no need) of anything among all beings for the brāhmaṇa (who sees the Self in them), above all.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he says the same.

Śaṅkara: as one who has done what is to be done has no use for a great well when water floods on every side, so for the brāhmaṇa who sees the Self in all beings there is, above all, no purpose at all; so the Lord Vāsudeva says (Gītā 3.18): ‘na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścid arthavyapāśrayaḥ’.

sanskrit.deva:
अहमेवास्मि वो माता पिता पुत्रोऽस्म्यहं पुनः ।
आत्माहमस्मि सर्वस्य यच्च नास्ति यदस्ति च ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aham evāsmi vo mātā pitā putro 'smy ahaṃ punaḥ |
ātmāham asmi sarvasya yac ca nāsti yad asti ca || 26 ||

lines.iast: aham evāsmi vo mātā pitā putro 'smy ahaṃ punaḥ
lines.deva: अहमेवास्मि वो माता पिता पुत्रोऽस्म्यहं पुनः

lines.iast: ātmāham asmi sarvasya yac ca nāsti yad asti ca
lines.deva: आत्माहमस्मि सर्वस्य यच्च नास्ति यदस्ति च

padaccheda.iast: aham eva asmi vaḥ mātā pitā putraḥ asmi aham punaḥ ātmā aham asmi sarvasya yat ca na asti yat asti ca
padaccheda.deva: अहम् एव अस्मि वः माता पिता पुत्रः अस्मि अहम् पुनः आत्मा अहम् अस्मि सर्वस्य यत् च न अस्ति यत् अस्ति च

translations.text: I am your mother, (I your) father; I am the son too. I am the Self of all, of what is not and of what is.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now, to make what has been said firm, he shows his own experience, as Vāmadeva and others did.

Śaṅkara: O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, I am your mother, who bore you; your father too am I; I am your son: I am Duryodhana and the rest. What more? I am the Self of all creatures; of what is not and of what is, I am the self.

sanskrit.deva:
पितामहोऽस्मि स्थविरः पिता पुत्रश्च भारत ।
ममैव यूयमात्मस्था न मे यूयं न चाप्यहम् ॥ २७ ॥

lines.deva: ममैव यूयमात्मस्था न मे यूयं न चाप्यहम्

padaccheda.iast: pitāmahaḥ asmi sthaviraḥ pitā putraḥ ca bhārata mama eva yūyam ātma-sthāḥ na me yūyam na ca api aham
padaccheda.deva: पितामहः अस्मि स्थविरः पिता पुत्रः च भारत मम एव यूयम् आत्म-स्थाः न मे यूयम् न च अपि अहम्

translations.text: I am the aged grandfather, the father and the son, O Bhārata. You stand in my Self alone; (yet in truth) you are not in me, nor I (in you).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: so far father and the rest have been shown as regards beings; now he shows himself as father and the rest as regards the deities.

Śaṅkara: the aged grandfather of Indra and the others, the beginningless supreme Self: that too am I. The father of Indra and the others, Hiraṇyagarbha: that too am I. So you stand in my Self alone. Yet, in the highest truth, you are none of you established in my self, nor am I established in you; so the Lord says (Gītā 9.4–5): ‘matsthāni sarvabhūtāni’.

sanskrit.deva:

ajaś caro divārātram atandrito 'haṃ māṃ vijñāya kavir āste prasannaḥ || 28 ||

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: (Yet) the Self alone is my abode, and my birth is the Self; I am woven across and along (through all), established in the ageless (my own greatness). Unborn, moving, unwearied day and night am I; knowing me, the wise man remains serene.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: although you do not stand in my self, nor I in you, yet —

Śaṅkara: the Self alone is the abode, the support; and birth is the Self: from this Self all has arisen (the śruti: ‘ātmaivedaṃ sarvam’). I alone stand woven across and along, the self of the world, your begetter. ajarapratiṣṭhaḥ: he stands in his own greatness, ageless, free of old age and death (the śruti: ‘sa bhagavaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ sve mahimni yadi vā na mahimni’). He does not gloss the second half (compare 4.18).
In the edition the bhāṣya on verses 28 and 29 is printed after the colophon of the adhyāya.

translations.text: Subtler than the subtle, of pure mind, I abide in all beings. (The knowers of Brahman) know the father of all beings, placed in the lotus (of the heart).

notes: Śaṅkara: subtler than the subtle. sumanāḥ: whose mind is good: free of passion, hatred, pride, envy, grief, delusion and the like, pure, of the form of Brahman, consciousness, being and bliss without a second. In all beings, all creatures, in the midst of the lotus of the heart, I abide as the Self.

Śaṅkara: so far his own experience has been shown. Now: not our experience alone is the evidence here; others know it so too. Sanaka, Sanandana, Vāmadeva and the other knowers of Brahman know the father of all creatures, the supreme Lord who begets them, placed in the lotus, in the midst of the lotus of the heart: they know the supreme Self as the self. The śruti shows their experience: in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, ‘tad dhaitat paśyann ṛṣir vāmadevaḥ pratipede 'haṃ manur abhavaṃ sūryaś ca’; in the Taittirīya, ‘etat sāma gāyann āste’, where the knower's own experience is shown by the singing of the sāman, to make known that he has gained his end; in the Chāndogya too, ‘tad dhāsya vijajñāv iti’; and in the Talavakāra the knower's own experience is shown with ‘aham annam’ and what follows.

Śaṅkara closes the bhāṣya with three verses of his own: meditating on the Lord, ever pure, awake and free, as the self, restraining the six senses, one stays unmoving; there is a reality, a mass of consciousness, the cause from which the world comes forth, not perishable, not born from it, that dispels darkness; denoted by the one word tat, ever immortal, spotless, the seer of the mind's activities, bliss: that I am, that I am.
